summary: Lolo NF lookout near Missoula built 1931 (firelookout.com says about 1932); occupied 1934-37; cabin burned in 1937 Miller Creek fire; dismantled 1947; listed Tower Gone.

facts.status_note: Dismantled after 1947; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower Gone.

events.note: Work started on a new lookout building; planned as a 20-foot tower with 14 by 14 foot living quarters.
Newspaper says the building was accomplished by May 1931; a 1947 report also gives 1931. firelookout.com says about 1932.
C. B. Pitts occupied the lookout in May; Stewart Griffiths occupied it in July.
Lewis Phillips, a forest school student, was employed as a lookout.
Miller Creek fire reached the peak in July; two men died.
Phillips's cabin burned per a 1937 newspaper; the wooden tower resisted the flames.
Lookout being dismantled after 16 years of service, per a September 1947 newspaper report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives about 1932 (after a 1929 log cabin); newspaper reports from 1930-1931 and a 1947 report give 1931. The story gives 1931 and notes the other date.
firelookout.com says 9 miles southeast of Missoula; the 1947 report says 10 air miles southeast of the city. The story gives nine to ten.
A July 1934 notice put the lookout southwest of Missoula; other sources put it southeast of Missoula or south of it. The story notes the notice.
The 1937 newspaper says the cabin burned and the wooden tower held. The 1947 report says the structure and tower were nearly burned, with the fire stopping 50 feet away. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The newspaper quotes come from the montanalookouts.weebly.com compilation, which transcribes newspapers; they were not checked against the originals. The build year and distance differ between sources, and the story shows both. No source describes the summit today. Searched once for Miller Peak history.
